components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The direct action for inspecting work or committing a reviewed brief.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A bounded alternative action that does not compete with the commissioning action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 50px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 0 21px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, #9eacb7); border-radius: var(--radius, 8px); background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #12202b); font-family: var(--body, sans-serif); font-size: 17px; font-weight: 650; line-height: 1.2; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out), color 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out), transform 140ms var(--ease-out, ease-out); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--accent, #0b4db8); color: var(--accent, #0b4db8); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #0b4db8); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

components.name: Project Brief Field
components.description: A reviewable brief field with explicit focus and invalid states.

components.name: Navigation Action

components.html: WorkStart a project
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 28px; font-family: var(--body, sans-serif); } .ds-nav a { min-height: 44px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; color: var(--ink, #12202b); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; transition: color 160ms var(--ease-out, ease-out), background-color 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out); } .ds-nav a:hover { color: var(--accent, #0b4db8); } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #0b4db8); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-nav .ds-nav-action { padding: 0 18px; border-radius: var(--radius, 8px); background: var(--ink, #12202b); color: var(--canvas, #f1f5f7); } .ds-nav .ds-nav-action:hover { background: var(--accent-hover, #083d93); color: var(--on-accent, #ffffff); }

components.name: Workflow Evidence Frame
components.description: A dark, ruled frame that presents real workflow imagery as inspectable evidence.
components.css: .ds-workflow-frame { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid var(--line, #c9d4dc); border-radius: var(--radius, 8px); background: #101a22; box-shadow: 0 18px 48px rgba(18, 32, 43, 0.08); font-family: var(--body, sans-serif); transition: border-color 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out), transform 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out); } .ds-workflow-frame:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong, #9eacb7); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-workflow-frame:focus-within { outline: 3px solid var(--accent, #0b4db8); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-workflow-canvas { min-height: 180px; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 22px; color: #cbd6dd; font-family: var(--data, monospace); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; background: linear-gradient(#16232d, #101a22); } .ds-workflow-frame figcaption { padding: 13px 16px; border-top: 1px solid #2c3942; color: #cbd6dd; font-size: 12px; }

components.css: .ds-verification-rail { margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); list-style: none; border-block: 1px solid var(--line, #c9d4dc); color: var(--ink, #12202b); font-family: var(--body, sans-serif); } .ds-verification-rail li { min-width: 0; padding: 24px 22px 26px; border-right: 1px solid var(--line, #c9d4dc); transition: background-color 170ms var(--ease-out, ease-out); } .ds-verification-rail li:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-verification-rail li:hover { background: var(--accent-soft, #e7eefb); } .ds-verification-rail strong, .ds-verification-rail span { display: block; } .ds-verification-rail strong { margin-bottom: 8px; color: var(--accent, #0b4db8); font-family: var(--data, monospace); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-verification-rail span { color: var(--muted, #506270); font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; }

narrative.overview:
The portfolio behaves like a concise technical dossier prepared before a system is commissioned. It is evidence-first and trust-first: strong claims sit beside the workflow image, test observation, known limit, and next human checkpoint that make each claim credible. Cool mineral surfaces create calm scrutiny, while commissioning blue marks the actions, labels, and system stages that deserve attention.

The interface is spacious but not ornamental. Broad editorial fields, documentary images, ruled evidence structures, and terse mono labels make the page feel inspected and accountable. Human presence is literal in the approved portrait and procedural in every review or handover step; the system must never drift into generic AI-agency spectacle, anonymous dark-tech gloss, or inflated proof.
keyCharacteristics: Evidence and limitation are presented as a matched pair.
Cool mineral surfaces carry most of the page; commissioning blue stays directional.
Real portraits and workflow captures outrank decorative illustration.
One gently rounded corner language keeps the dossier coherent.
Dense operational detail is separated by rules, spacing, and mono evidence labels.
Motion is brief, interruptible, and absent when reduced motion is requested.

rules.name: The Commissioning Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue points to action, evidence, state, or system sequence; it is never sprayed across passive decoration.

rules.name: The Evidence State Rule
rules.body: Red and green communicate observed form or submission state only, never project category or personality.

rules.name: The Mineral Continuity Rule
rules.body: Light and dark themes preserve the same semantic hierarchy rather than becoming separate visual identities.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo states the proposition, Atkinson explains it, and Azeret records evidence; do not swap these roles for novelty.

rules.name: The Balanced Claim Rule
rules.body: Large headings use tight leading and balanced wrapping, while explanatory copy stays comfortably spaced and measure-limited.

rules.name: The Inspection Order Rule
rules.body: Responsive collapse preserves reading order—claim, image, system path, observed result, known limit, next test—so mobile never separates proof from context.

rules.name: The Broad Field Rule
rules.body: Empty space is part of the evidence hierarchy; do not fill the 96px–152px section rhythm with decorative modules.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If a one-pixel rule or tonal shift explains the boundary, do not add a shadow.

rules.name: The Consequence Rule
rules.body: Elevation marks surfaces where the visitor inspects identity, navigation, evidence, or their own submitted information.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: Use the established 8px corner wherever a contained surface needs rounding; do not introduce a second soft-card radius.

rules.name: The No Pill Rule
rules.body: Labels and metadata remain typographic or rule-bound, not capsule-shaped badges.

dos: Do pair every consequential claim with observed evidence, a known limit, or a next test.
Do use commissioning blue for direction and verification cues, not as ambient decoration.
Do preserve the approved portrait and real workflow imagery as the dominant visual proof.
Do maintain the 8px dossier radius, one-pixel mineral rules, and generous section rhythm.
Do preserve visible focus, 44px touch targets, reduced-motion behavior, and semantic light/dark parity.
Do keep human review, confirmation, and handover checkpoints visible in system narratives.
donts: Don't turn the portfolio into a generic AI-agency card grid, neon tech spectacle, or anonymous dark dashboard.
Don't imply client deployment, operational savings, or production readiness when the evidence only supports a prototype or personal system.
Don't hide limitations below decorative imagery or detach them from the result they qualify.
Don't add pill badges, gradient fills, ornamental glows, or competing accent colors.
Don't replace workflow captures with abstract AI illustrations when real system evidence exists.
Don't animate structural content continuously; use only brief entry and state transitions, and honor reduced-motion preferences.
